round_interpretation: All 69 historical masks have complete matched three-seed results. Sixteen points are nondominated. The seven-input trend/lag/HY-z model has the highest Sharpe (0.535004), IC 0.150000 and NLL -2.590394. The seven-input no-lag rate/TIPS model has higher IC 0.261111 and similar Sharpe 0.532632 but worse NLL -2.438584. Density anchors retain lag and broader rate inputs, including duplicate Treasury-level names. The novelty gate showed that replacing the credit parent's HY z-score with the absolute level was already tested and was worse on all three aggregate objectives, so that repeat was replaced with a shared-local-basis experiment. This round tests lag and local pruning in the credit model, individual TIPS/rate removals in the no-lag model, a bridge combining their macro information, local volatility, and exact-definition redundancy in the density anchor. No conclusion that lag must be kept or removed is imposed.
default_expected_tradeoff: Evaluate all three objectives, seed dispersion and coverage; count removed/added inputs explicitly without treating count or narrow intervals as an extra objective.
default_falsification: A dominated or otherwise noncompetitive outcome does not support the stated conditional simplification or transfer. A new nondominated tradeoff remains reportable rather than being rejected by a hidden NLL/Sharpe guardrail.

candidates.name: credit_sharpe_parent_without_lag
candidates.hypothesis: Genuine HY state plus the richer local trend basis may make recent excess-return lag unnecessary in the strongest repaired-data Sharpe model; test the exact pair under the same 84-month history.

candidates.name: credit_sharpe_parent_without_long_momentum
candidates.hypothesis: Annual momentum and acceleration may substitute for long-horizon momentum once the HY z-score is present, reducing the compact credit model by one input.

candidates.name: credit_sharpe_parent_without_global_rank
candidates.hypothesis: The common-universe rank may add less information than local trend and repaired credit state in this fixed-income context; do not infer a shared core rank from equity inclusion alone.

candidates.name: credit_parent_with_shared_equity_local_basis
candidates.hypothesis: A four-input local basis shared with both equity families may combine with the useful HY z-score as a compact five-input fixed-income hypothesis. This changes the representation as a whole; the separate exact lag-removal test, not this transfer, determines conditional lag evidence.

candidates.name: no_lag_rate_parent_without_one_month_tips_return
candidates.hypothesis: The trailing TIPS-return proxy and nominal yield may preserve the no-lag model's useful rate state without noisy one-month SCHP return.

candidates.name: no_lag_rate_parent_without_three_month_tips_proxy
candidates.hypothesis: The one-month SCHP return and nominal yield may be sufficient without the trailing three-month proxy; the reciprocal test identifies their conditional complementarity.

candidates.name: no_lag_rate_parent_without_nominal_yield
candidates.hypothesis: The TIPS-return representations may carry the useful state without a Treasury-level input, or this removal may establish why a nominal yield belongs in a shared feature core.

candidates.name: no_lag_rate_parent_without_return_autocorrelation
candidates.hypothesis: Rate/TIPS context may substitute for the local autocorrelation signal while preserving the no-lag model's ranking advantage.

candidates.name: no_lag_rate_parent_plus_hy_zscore
candidates.hypothesis: Combine the credit information from the best-Sharpe model with the high-IC no-lag rate model, testing whether their advantages can coexist without restoring recent-return lag.

candidates.name: no_lag_rate_parent_plus_local_realized_volatility
candidates.hypothesis: Task-specific realized volatility may address the no-lag rate model's density weakness without importing a broad risk block or simply shrinking predictive intervals.

candidates.name: density_anchor_without_duplicate_nominal_yield_name
candidates.hypothesis: The repaired tnote10y and y10_nominal columns are bitwise-identical; remove one explicit axis while measuring the finite-budget GP geometry and prior effects rather than assuming output invariance.

candidates.name: density_anchor_with_minimal_equivalent_curve_basis
candidates.hypothesis: After removing the duplicate yield name, tnote10y and term_spread algebraically contain the bill-rate information; test a two-input representation reduction without claiming a nonlinear GP is automatically invariant.
